**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
The exec probe timeout errors are converted into Unknown Result with error returned, causing kubelet throws away the result and the container isn't restarted as expected. Like http and tcp probes, timeout errors should be converted into Failure Result with no error returned.

issue_context.title: exec probe timeout failures cannot trigger container restart
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
When using containerd as CRI runtime, a Pod with exec liveness probe cannot be restarted by timeout errors, though the errors were detected and liveness probe events were recorded correctly:
```
  Normal   Created    2m6s                kubelet, k8s-01    Created container test
  Normal   Started    2m6s                kubelet, k8s-01    Started container test
  Warning  Unhealthy  2s (x12 over 112s)  kubelet, k8s-01    Liveness probe errored: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = failed to exec in container: timeout 2s exceeded: context deadline exceeded
```
```
Containers:
  test:
    Container ID:  containerd://399a7b6db1b32cc49df9723a9f30217b3d0e9bbc1424272c0a2fdc293ab74bb6
    Image:         nginx
    Image ID:      docker.io/library/nginx@sha256:21f32f6c08406306d822a0e6e8b7dc81f53f336570e852e25fbe1e3e3d0d0133
    Port:          <none>
    Host Port:     <none>
    Command:
      sleep
      3600
    State:          Running
      Started:      Wed, 24 Jun 2020 04:46:06 -0700
    Ready:          True
    Restart Count:  0
    Liveness:       exec [sleep 4] delay=0s timeout=2s period=10s #success=1 #failure=3
    Environment:    <none>
    Mounts:
      /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount from default-token-24hfm (ro)
```

The reason is the errors other than `exec.ExitError` are converted into `Unknown` Result with error returned, causing kubelet throws away the result.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4de511a4cfdb8e49e804be18245911bf3270fb2f/pkg/probe/exec/exec.go#L61-L70

**What you expected to happen**:
Like http and tcp probes, exec timeout errors should be converted as `Failure` Result and should trigger restarting container.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Use containerd as CRI
2. Create a Pod and make its exec probe timeout
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: testpod
spec:
  restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: nginx
    command:
      - sleep
      - "3600"
    livenessProbe:
      timeoutSeconds: 2
      exec:
        command:
        - sleep
        - "4"
```
The Liveness probe error events will be generated but the container won't be restarted.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.18.3
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others: containerd v1.3.4

Any workarounds?  This is causing one of my pods to fail thousands of checks but stay up `Warning  Unhealthy  2m59s (x11089 over 15h)`

> Any workarounds? This is causing one of my pods to fail thousands of checks but stay up `Warning Unhealthy 2m59s (x11089 over 15h)`

A workaround is using `timeout` to wrap the exec command so that the command can fail with a non-zero exit code which is respected by the kubelet probe code. For example:
```
    livenessProbe:
      timeoutSeconds: 3 # If the desired timeout is greater than 1 second, this value must be specified and greater than the timeout specified in exec command so that that one will fail first.
      exec:
        command:
        - timeout
        - "2"
        - <THE REAL COMMAND>
```

BTW, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94115 should fix this.

review_comments:
this code assumes that timeout will be implemented at grpc layer, not inside the containerD. It introduces tight coupling between with the implementation.

Did you check if `exec.Exited()` was set to `false` in case of timeout?

Thanks for the review.
containerd implements the timeout with context timeout and converts the `context.DeadlineExceeded` to grpc `DeadlineExceeded` as response. There is no `ExecSyncResponse` in case of timeout.
https://github.com/containerd/cri/blob/09d6426f33cac217528158ddc6d254ca7d597a7b/pkg/server/container_execsync.go#L171
https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/c75180740937d4b2d44b9c1edc1c27b208e66e32/errdefs/grpc.go#L61-L62

I also thought it's too coupled to check grpc error here but didn't find a proper error struct to represent the timeout error.
How about this option:
At rpc client side, convert grpc DeadlineExceeded to `context.DeadlineExceeded` or a new error struct that implements `ExitError`, or the `CodeExitError` if it's acceptable. If `context.DeadlineExceeded`, the `Probe` method needs to convert it to `Failure` result.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4de511a4cfdb8e49e804be18245911bf3270fb2f/pkg/kubelet/cri/remote/remote_runtime.go#L387-L391

There was a discussion at sig node meeting lately. And mentioned this comment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92057#issuecomment-644915304 I think it's worth understanding if the timeout was passed correctly to containerd. This may be a better fix.

It looks like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92057#issuecomment-644915304 was talking about lifecycle event hander, not probe handler?
For probe handler, I think it's passed to container runtime correctly:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e7ca64fbe16d0c4b6c7b36aecde9cd75042b2828/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go#L157-L161
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e7ca64fbe16d0c4b6c7b36aecde9cd75042b2828/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container.go#L826-L827
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e7ca64fbe16d0c4b6c7b36aecde9cd75042b2828/pkg/kubelet/cri/remote/remote_runtime.go#L382-L387

Besides, the probe failure event in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92464#issue-644561356 `Liveness probe errored: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = failed to exec in container: timeout 2s exceeded: context deadline exceeded` has the configured timeout `2s`, which was returned by containerd:
https://github.com/containerd/cri/blob/master/pkg/server/container_execsync.go#L171

Thank you for all the context. The fact that grpc timeout creeped all the way here confused me. I like your previous comment on converting grpc code back to some non-grpc failure on CRI side. Sounds like a good solution. 

@dchen1107 @yujuhong what do you think?
